ai.definition: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is a software technology that uses software robots, or 'bots,' to automate repetitive, rules-based tasks typically performed by humans in various business processes.
ai.howItWorks: Bots are programmed to mimic human interactions with digital systems, such as clicking buttons and typing text into fields. They can operate on both the front-end (user interface) and back-end of applications, performing actions like data entry, form filling, and report generation.
ai.problemSolved: RPA addresses inefficiencies in manual processes by automating them, reducing errors, and freeing up human workers for more complex tasks.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing is not a primary aspect of RPA. Instead, it involves software development and deployment.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes defining the workflow, selecting appropriate RPA tools, scripting actions, testing bots in a sandbox environment, and deploying them to production systems.
ai.costDrivers: Costs are driven by the complexity of workflows, licensing fees for RPA software, integration with existing systems, and training staff on new processes.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: growing adoption across industries as businesses seek to optimize operations through automation.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by industry and region. Compliance is a key consideration for RPA implementation in sectors like finance, healthcare, and government where data privacy and security are paramount.
ai.risks: Risks include integration challenges with legacy systems, potential job displacement, cybersecurity threats to data integrity, and the need for ongoing maintenance and updates.
ai.profitability: Profitability depends on the specific business case. Successful implementations can lead to cost savings, increased efficiency, and improved customer satisfaction, but ROI varies widely.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include more advanced AI capabilities like natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML), enabling bots to handle more complex tasks and decision-making processes.

glossary.def: Software programs designed to automate repetitive tasks.
A sequence of steps or processes that are carried out in a specific order.

subsystems.name: Bot authoring studio
subsystems.role: lets developers and business users design automation workflows without deep programming.

subsystems.name: Execution engine
subsystems.role: runs bots and controls their interactions with applications and the operating system.

subsystems.name: Integration layer
subsystems.role: connects bots to databases, APIs, files, and enterprise systems.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and control room
subsystems.role: central management for deploying, scheduling, and monitoring bots at scale.

subsystems.name: Cognitive services
subsystems.role: extends automation to unstructured data and judgment-based tasks.

subsystems.name: Security and governance
subsystems.role: ensures bots operate within compliance and access controls.

buildSteps.title: Identify and prioritize processes
buildSteps.detail: Analyse business processes for high-volume, repetitive, rule-based steps that are stable and low-risk.

buildSteps.title: Map the process in detail
buildSteps.detail: Document each step, decision point, exception, and system interaction to define the automation logic.

buildSteps.title: Design the bot workflow
buildSteps.detail: Use a visual designer to lay out actions, loops, conditions, and error handling.

buildSteps.title: Develop and configure the bot
buildSteps.detail: Build the automation using recorders, drag-and-drop activities, or code; connect to applications via UI or APIs.

buildSteps.title: Test in a sandbox
buildSteps.detail: Run the bot against test data, verify outputs, and handle edge cases and failures.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and schedule
buildSteps.detail: Publish the bot to the control room, set triggers (time, event), and assign credentials securely.

buildSteps.title: Monitor, maintain, and scale
buildSteps.detail: Track bot performance, update automations when underlying applications change, and add AI for unstructured data.

pathway.milestone: rule-based automation for structured, repetitive tasks in finance, HR, and operations
pathway.unlocks: cost reduction and error reduction for well-defined processes.

pathway.milestone: intelligent automation combining RPA with AI for semi-structured and unstructured data
pathway.unlocks: automation of document-heavy workflows like invoice processing and customer emails.

pathway.milestone: process mining and task mining to discover automation opportunities from system logs
pathway.unlocks: faster, data-driven selection of processes to automate.

pathway.milestone: autonomous agents that learn, adapt to UI changes, and make simple decisions
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end automation of complex, multi-step business processes with minimal human intervention.
